title: The chronolex extension of an article (produces.extensions.chronolex) v0.3.0
description: What an article of a law or a policy says for chronolexography, in its own namespace under produces.extensions (RFC-022 sec. 3.2): the facts it brings into being (establishes), how it reads its own parameters from a chronicle (reads), and, in implementing policy only, the channels of the actor, what each supplies to a submission and the authorities it acts for under mandate (RFC-047). The law schema leaves extensions open; the runtime validates this block against this schema when it loads the corpus.

reads.description: One reading, or one per paragraph that reads differently; each becomes a lexostatus named after the article (<regulation>#<article>, with ' lid <n>' for a paragraph).

channels.description: The channels of the actor, by id; only in implementing policy that names a competent authority. The technique of each is in the deployment (channels.yaml).

supplies.description: Per channel what it puts into a submission, per field of the gram: a field of the channel, the route it came in by ($channel) or, through a portal only, the day it was submitted ($submitted_on).

mandates.description: Authorities on whose behalf the actor also acts, under mandate.

path.description: A field path under the fields of a gram; a path covers everything below it.

establishment.description: A fact the article brings into being, as an event of a chronicle (event), or the extension of a fact that another article establishes (extends).

event.description: The event this article establishes, by its name in the chronicle.

extends.description: The event (by name) that this article extends, or the submission its hook applies to ({submission: <STAGE>}).

type.description: The type of the gram, open vocabulary (RFC-022 sec. 1).

legal_basis.description: The legal basis the gram carries. Without it: the article itself for an event; for an extension the legal basis of the origin of each field it declares.

effective_at.description: Why the effective_at counts in law, and which piece of data it is: a parameter of this article or a field of the gram; neither means the moment of receipt.

only.description: Only when a submitted value states the moment (stated), or only when nothing states it and the recording counts (recorded). Without it: always.

fields.description: The fields of the gram: a keyword (outputs: the outputs of this article; stage: what the stage requires and the outputs of its hooks; parameters: the parameters of this article that a party or the channel supplies), a list of field paths, named parameters, or field paths with their type.

aliases.description: Name bridge: under which name another article reads a field of this gram (<name at the reader>: <field of the gram>).

prefill.description: Fields a register may fill in beforehand: per field the output of the regulation that knows it (by default the regulation of this article).

stage.description: A stage of the procedure (RFC-008), as the law names it.

type.description: A parameter type of the law schema.

origin.description: Who supplies the field, in the shape of an origin in the law schema; without it the field is input.

reading.description: How the article reads its own parameters from the chronicle, in the vocabulary of the reduction (lexostatus.json).

paragraph.description: The paragraph that carries this reading, if the article has more readings.

from.description: Which grams the article reads, if it picks one (with pick).

decision.description: The article reads the grams of the decision it is asked for.

parameters.description: Per parameter of this article its derivation, optionally with from (which grams) and legal_basis (without: this article). The runtime checks each derivation against the reduction vocabulary.

kind.description: What the channel is for; it decides the routes of its role: a portal to apply, the handling of cases, or a counter that enters an application on behalf of the applicant.

role.description: The role that logs in through it; without it: the channel id.

identifies.description: The fields of the login: names, or per name the legal basis of the rule that knows the value and its form.

owner.description: The field of the submission that designates who follows a case.

submits.description: The article whose submission this portal records (<regulation>#<article>).

assesses.description: The output of the submitted article that the portal assesses before submitting.

offers.description: What the portal offers: an output of a regulation, optionally with the outputs of that regulation for a deadline, the windows on offer, the first day of a window and the first day an application for it can come in.

form.description: The form document that gives the portal order, groups and labels (form.json); document relative to the corpus root.

legal_basis.description: One legal basis or more; the first is the basis of the role.
